While famous as a morning-after remedy, people also eat it as a filling everyday meal.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXRi85HSTv4xyhU559XxQ_n_FDc3JpXNEe7si-urzBA9GsyqClKiTdDbZAvw_s8Dy6wRr1QMmfsWnBHkY3uPn7Fu64EaxgOUSkXjr5JL9gFu3tsi1bsH4nHL6xtbv1Lek)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXqRGEGMsg6DzUpW7aYC8Up0K7XqqtPWwvb_3FQAFucdpN6Qkqo_McNY1J9i5bBcqwwos0TYtAw2Snc3QZNGunZ9LkoBDSYYAFNyPScdEk1rxdt0O3U8JIkkPMpRKmQEm5kDfolu-K)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXX0nMUgwNNTEVPz68rC1yEZTAM7h8IeEqgR9CIV0InWK242TLhTDVkI2RtB7AgbDMwEHE0HkesHsO-cMV3pkxqPKAmy9W1qOzRZ6tIk420lCNzr6GxXfm1mJrE9SfEjZCA4IHCB5lA2BRfvUUItiHynlg)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnwEBxCJF18l8C4FrD6bK90WQRVAuBH-oeX3saY39FWN69UNk0kQFtQQFDXyeJhE2BrC0huY8ALlGNuszYzjgtTAkl_IsVxGys1Qepp3QX0O2pSZ2RsLOH1ZeAF4NiUcJnBnUqfo8RtE92Zp0HzRX7gXWyjuvP5jwgacpPaDKwG_6ip7fOafzC_Czt5oZjS1HHi1gUhtyyjrn0SUk5qoAsZg)

#### Taste & Common Ingredients

Haejang-guk is typically savory, rich, and umami-heavy, often with a spicy kick. Depending on the specific style, key ingredients include:[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14NszoGFrlnOgTPeOWZbuCsGGKHhsOKOTMJLpgO9gYH5HWVzugZ7GXkQvFeV6JkaQ7JvLzklEozkn-83nbsN8R9ALkN9DcVvDoQC37PthjHZwhOiKzzD80wL3rw-gcSKGvhnWlyBMioZPdTOHcf9W5rRKelq6jFkYwuV_V5bBqY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXRji_mJmHR1ogWnWHbc0unO4vg7HEMfz4AL59w24YmM8j5K7isr_CKCHM2QSG0Omrp_DNVb46W5l_GHM-FlFiEedOc7W_Njvwi9k091fP_NbNSPnZ35YqpRcCwGsaO6mhJZg)

- **Broth & Paste:** Beef bone broth, pork spine broth, or light seafood/vegetable broths seasoned with *doenjang* (fermented soybean paste), garlic, *gochugaru* (Korean chili flakes), or *gochujang* (chili paste).
- **Vegetables:** Napa cabbage (or dried outer cabbage leaves called *ugeoji* ), Korean radish, bean sprouts (*kongnamul* ), and green onions.
- **Proteins:** Sliced beef, tripe, congealed ox blood (*seonji* ), pork backbone, or dried pollack.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXSydYV0kNeue_d5_rtq_MJsV3uuVs6FE-PBeJ0KX7bIbKmx8t0B_OrWw4Ag4_3gkpAziNovas2CXo6S6-KWF_xWuKdzM80ji27SKba3VW2yPJKI8tq92Pbsx4tbDjSL0ZZGBLbBHX)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14NszoGFrlnOgTPeOWZbuCsGGKHhsOKOTMJLpgO9gYH5HWVzugZ7GXkQvFeV6JkaQ7JvLzklEozkn-83nbsN8R9ALkN9DcVvDoQC37PthjHZwhOiKzzD80wL3rw-gcSKGvhnWlyBMioZPdTOHcf9W5rRKelq6jFkYwuV_V5bBqY)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXRji_mJmHR1ogWnWHbc0unO4vg7HEMfz4AL59w24YmM8j5K7isr_CKCHM2QSG0Omrp_DNVb46W5l_GHM-FlFiEedOc7W_Njvwi9k091fP_NbNSPnZ35YqpRcCwGsaO6mhJZg)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnwEBxCJF18l8C4FrD6bK90WQRVAuBH-oeX3saY39FWN69UNk0kQFtQQFDXyeJhE2BrC0huY8ALlGNuszYzjgtTAkl_IsVxGys1Qepp3QX0O2pSZ2RsLOH1ZeAF4NiUcJnBnUqfo8RtE92Zp0HzRX7gXWyjuvP5jwgacpPaDKwG_6ip7fOafzC_Czt5oZjS1HHi1gUhtyyjrn0SUk5qoAsZg)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXRi85HSTv4xyhU559XxQ_n_FDc3JpXNEe7si-urzBA9GsyqClKiTdDbZAvw_s8Dy6wRr1QMmfsWnBHkY3uPn7Fu64EaxgOUSkXjr5JL9gFu3tsi1bsH4nHL6xtbv1Lek)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF17wtXavEL81NH8nbvcLpv8i2uqWWYX1bVV5AHEBvkloJchrTx3kNNbGgfUklPTUtR1p_MvYPjBdtZhDNHHkedZY4-uDZlHSzqjiFZdYLU-W2OiXyyrkjfM1ZeFuzvDY6NWHzvzr7XIbdfjfr4dhTrQ-VFhHzTSuZAm_rKTGfF_saW79d_YKbERErXyA8Q75l3vYt59thEMtA)

### Popular Varieties
Because "haejang-guk" covers many hangover soups, bowls vary widely by region and restaurant:[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXRi85HSTv4xyhU559XxQ_n_FDc3JpXNEe7si-urzBA9GsyqClKiTdDbZAvw_s8Dy6wRr1QMmfsWnBHkY3uPn7Fu64EaxgOUSkXjr5JL9gFu3tsi1bsH4nHL6xtbv1Lek)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXX0nMUgwNNTEVPz68rC1yEZTAM7h8IeEqgR9CIV0InWK242TLhTDVkI2RtB7AgbDMwEHE0HkesHsO-cMV3pkxqPKAmy9W1qOzRZ6tIk420lCNzr6GxXfm1mJrE9SfEjZCA4IHCB5lA2BRfvUUItiHynlg)

- **Seonji-guk (선지국):** Made with congealed ox blood (similar to black pudding), cabbage, radish, and bean sprouts in a savory or spicy broth.
- **Ppyeo-haejangguk / Gamjatang (뼈해장국):** Built around meaty pork spine bones, cabbage, and often perilla seed powder.
- **Kongnamul-gukbap (콩나물국밥):** A lighter, clear bean sprout soup served with rice, often popular in Jeonju.
- **Hwangtae-guk / Bugeotguk (황태국 / 북어국):** A milder soup made with dried pollack.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF16u0hFtbYAZ07Xtcjha8SnGEoxj7DnEhaCiAXOpOs_b9BDObSOd1CRtjkbaXodZmwnOcQn0S0aBO8eu3gJHDACePyEIfmr4tvMLCVUChjLABNbxGAII02auNM-tVARcZZt7WLt2Xcl_lW_k120SD7lGHrBFqWACyA5vc8TxE-QOPbmi5Ikg00lkcMC4)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXRi85HSTv4xyhU559XxQ_n_FDc3JpXNEe7si-urzBA9GsyqClKiTdDbZAvw_s8Dy6wRr1QMmfsWnBHkY3uPn7Fu64EaxgOUSkXjr5JL9gFu3tsi1bsH4nHL6xtbv1Lek)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF12cTHwhcVMR9RdrTaEWDHl_6_1iEO4wjd1kzgJ0xueiaJ3-Lg9Q9C4is5744yNZ4Ke1TQOFTf4_iyA032PnKVdwS3P2zxvHziBxua9PPdtESprePNfskg3-Ibq7kLV3pkpv8O-RNqKwXNX_Q5HaPw727itYyvXSwTYZnJVS_2Of1KGkc)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF15R76jKVCLB6XOoYPQoWpnX0R8UZG9ORtOQCNmNZD7p1HL00D21pv4BoIvBhFHXcUfwdrkegeTvXWfwrWrmVbOuGrVKmi-GMu0aEb4XTofRQVf7s4mIfrSrFHWso3xOE0WuQqyjmVXP-e-Pd4Jt6A3_UwPiN7_ayrMsTgev9VJRaT9abBwDe)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnwEBxCJF18l8C4FrD6bK90WQRVAuBH-oeX3saY39FWN69UNk0kQFtQQFDXyeJhE2BrC0huY8ALlGNuszYzjgtTAkl_IsVxGys1Qepp3QX0O2pSZ2RsLOH1ZeAF4NiUcJnBnUqfo8RtE92Zp0HzRX7gXWyjuvP5jwgacpPaDKwG_6ip7fOafzC_Czt5oZjS1HHi1gUhtyyjrn0SUk5qoAsZg)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXX93M81wDCWCKIyj_qYEzVL9FVVbHA0ju1g423eckCuPyWUwu7AcMxLe3dpHf-5CYmMxbN9X8PbrTaqrL-MMzEis-9p1jDAQwNDrF0FIy1QsHxnScsNBY4K8v5o1cTStaJWFK-XW44Zi8zuPKcfw)

### Origins & History
A precursor called *seongjutang* ("soup to get sober") appears in the late Goryeo-era text *Nogeoldae* . Over centuries, taverns and street stalls served warming broths to travelers, laborers, and late-night drinkers. In Seoul, areas like Cheongjin-dong became famous for haejang-guk restaurants such as [Cheongjinok](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXRi85HSTv4xyhU559XxQ_n_FDc3JpXNEe7si-urzBA9GsyqClKiTdDbZAvw_s8Dy6wRr1QMmfsWnBHkY3uPn7Fu64EaxgOUSkXjr5JL9gFu3tsi1bsH4nHL6xtbv1Lek).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHEIkXXRi85HSTv4xyhU559XxQ_n_FDc3JpXNEe7si-urzBA9GsyqClKiTdDbZAvw_s8Dy6wRr1QMmfsWnBHkY3uPn7Fu64EaxgOUSkXjr5JL9gFu3tsi1bsH4nHL6xtbv1Lek)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESpwEBxCJF11uNtnDeEx-2yJy7SGinPCUJgUtwKhSdooX2I3qrgpnBmn_11BCCsoul4U16LISf45kl4sy1K02O42FiytRn1pF0VkjDbPYvtxcGuRVuAqi0XRGtFvnQ5Le9xez7Y7LA_54-RpRpegLyVEWwjVqUfnFjtHN4E3-SZoLuFSkI8rnJbQvRgf7E0bL5fK6WDexYQ-mjlDzaIdR5iQO6TmFs2N2DWg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF15R76jKVCLB6XOoYPQoWpnX0R8UZG9ORtOQCNmNZD7p1HL00D21pv4BoIvBhFHXcUfwdrkegeTvXWfwrWrmVbOuGrVKmi-GMu0aEb4XTofRQVf7s4mIfrSrFHWso3xOE0WuQqyjmVXP-e-Pd4Jt6A3_UwPiN7_ayrMsTgev9VJRaT9abBwDe)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXZnkQNcJ0XQN9TAlESvWcarAau8GanYXjiKKINY1cuUg5rAM6AK_Tx4N7I7JD1NXnWHideq2KFIV-34X-r3BwRIhoKVePrqoKJ_FjWY9KT7CWkRTFWHA0ANFZbVUAwoe1xmukO2ZbooKa_FNaQzTL)To see how a classic bone-based version comes together at home, check out [Maangchi](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXqRGEGMsg6DzUpW7aYC8Up0K7XqqtPWwvb_3FQAFucdpN6Qkqo_McNY1J9i5bBcqwwos0TYtAw2Snc3QZNGunZ9LkoBDSYYAFNyPScdEk1rxdt0O3U8JIkkPMpRKmQEm5kDfolu-K) for a step-by-step *ppyeo-haejangguk* recipe and video. Users on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF17wtXavEL81NH8nbvcLpv8i2uqWWYX1bVV5AHEBvkloJchrTx3kNNbGgfUklPTUtR1p_MvYPjBdtZhDNHHkedZY4-uDZlHSzqjiFZdYLU-W2OiXyyrkjfM1ZeFuzvDY6NWHzvzr7XIbdfjfr4dhTrQ-VFhHzTSuZAm_rKTGfF_saW79d_YKbERErXyA8Q75l3vYt59thEMtA) also reach a consensus that *Yangpyeong haejangguk* —featuring beef tripe and *seonji* —is a standout regional style that is tricky to replicate at home.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXqRGEGMsg6DzUpW7aYC8Up0K7XqqtPWwvb_3FQAFucdpN6Qkqo_McNY1J9i5bBcqwwos0TYtAw2Snc3QZNGunZ9LkoBDSYYAFNyPScdEk1rxdt0O3U8JIkkPMpRKmQEm5kDfolu-K)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF17wtXavEL81NH8nbvcLpv8i2uqWWYX1bVV5AHEBvkloJchrTx3kNNbGgfUklPTUtR1p_MvYPjBdtZhDNHHkedZY4-uDZlHSzqjiFZdYLU-W2OiXyyrkjfM1ZeFuzvDY6NWHzvzr7XIbdfjfr4dhTrQ-VFhHzTSuZAm_rKTGfF_saW79d_YKbERErXyA8Q75l3vYt59thEMtA)Would you like a **recipe** for a specific style (such as **pork bone**, **beef and cabbage** , or **bean sprout** ), or are you looking for **restaurant recommendations** in a specific city?

items.text: Seonji-guk (선지국): Made with congealed ox blood (similar to black pudding), cabbage, radish, and bean sprouts in a savory or spicy broth. Ppyeo-haejangguk / Gamjatang (뼈해장국): Built around meaty pork spine bones, cabbage, and often perilla seed powder. Kongnamul-gukbap (콩나물국밥): A lighter, clear bean sprout soup served with rice, often popular in Jeonju. Hwangtae-guk / Bugeotguk (황태국 / 북어국): A milder soup made with dried pollack.
items.markdown:
- **Seonji-guk (선지국):** Made with congealed ox blood (similar to black pudding), cabbage, radish, and bean sprouts in a savory or spicy broth.
- **Ppyeo-haejangguk / Gamjatang (뼈해장국):** Built around meaty pork spine bones, cabbage, and often perilla seed powder.
- **Kongnamul-gukbap (콩나물국밥):** A lighter, clear bean sprout soup served with rice, often popular in Jeonju.

items.title: Origins & History
items.text: A precursor called seongjutang ("soup to get sober") appears in the late Goryeo-era text Nogeoldae. Over centuries, taverns and street stalls served warming broths to travelers, laborers, and late-night drinkers. In Seoul, areas like Cheongjin-dong became famous for haejang-guk restaurants such as Cheongjinok.
